verified_facts.note: Publicly announced endorsements during campaign period

points_of_disagreement: Whether Pérez's 20-year run without opposition represents healthy institutional continuity or democratic deficit
Whether the 65% vote share constitutes a strong mandate or a weakened position (given the first-ever serious challenger)
Whether Mourinho + €150m Galáctico strategy or Klopp + Haaland vision better addresses Real Madrid's sporting needs
Whether the 5% privatization stake represents necessary modernization or a threat to member-ownership identity
Whether Riquelme's 35% represents a protest vote against incumbency or genuine support for an alternative vision
Whether the absence of Real Madrid players from Spain's World Cup squad reflects Pérez's global-brand strategy or broader squad-building factors
Whether strict candidacy barriers (20-year membership, 15% budget guarantee) protect institutional stability or entrench power
Whether Riquelme's campaign promises (Haaland, Klopp) were credible commitments or 'transfer theater' designed to compete with Pérez's spectacle
shared_foundation.summary: All framings accept that Pérez defeated Riquelme 65%–35% in Real Madrid's first contested election in 20 years, with Mourinho confirmed as manager, a 5% privatization stake planned, and Spain's World Cup squad containing no Real Madrid players. The disagreement centers entirely on how to interpret these facts: as validation of Pérez's legacy and sporting vision, or as evidence of democratic deficit, institutional entrenchment, and a club at a crossroads between member-ownership and privatization.

framings.name: Democratic Legitimacy & Accountability
framings.question: Was this election genuinely democratic, and does Pérez's re-election reflect authentic member will?
framings.key_claim: After 20 years of running unopposed, Pérez's first contested election in two decades raises questions about whether Real Madrid's governance structure enables real democratic accountability.
framings.description: This framing focuses on the structural conditions of the election itself — the 20-year gap without a contested vote, the strict candidacy requirements, the annulled postal ballots, and Riquelme's pre-election complaints about the electoral roll. It asks whether the result reflects genuine member democracy or an incumbency advantage baked into the rules.
framings.emphasizes: The 20-year absence of contested elections, strict candidacy barriers (20-year membership, 15% budget guarantee), annulment of ~1,000 postal votes, Riquelme's pre-vote complaints about the electoral register, and Pérez's refusal to debate.
framings.downplays: Pérez's decisive 65%-35% margin, the Electoral Board's formal rebuttal of Riquelme's complaints, and the fact that both candidacies were certified as valid.

framings.name: Sporting Performance & Managerial Vision
framings.question: Which presidential vision — Mourinho or Klopp, Galácticos or Spanish identity — offers the best path back to trophies?
framings.key_claim: Pérez's re-election locks in a Mourinho-led, Galáctico-transfer strategy to end a two-season trophy drought, while Riquelme's defeated Klopp-and-Haaland vision represented a generational alternative.
framings.description: The dominant framing in mainstream sports media: the election as a sporting referendum on how to rebuild a trophy-less Real Madrid. Coverage centers on the competing managerial and transfer promises — Mourinho vs. Klopp, Konaté/Dumfries vs. Haaland/Rodri — and what Pérez's win means for the squad.
framings.emphasizes: Mourinho's confirmed return, the €150m Galáctico pledge, Konaté and Dumfries signings, the two-season trophy drought, and Riquelme's Klopp/Haaland promises.
framings.downplays: Governance, ownership structure, and electoral process questions; treats the election primarily as a sporting management decision.

framings.name: Ownership Identity & Privatization Threat
framings.question: Does Pérez's re-election and his 5% stake sale plan endanger Real Madrid's century-old member-owned identity?
framings.key_claim: Pérez's plan to sell a 5% stake to a private investor represents the first crack in Real Madrid's 124-year member-ownership model, and his re-election makes that structural shift imminent.
framings.description: This framing treats the election as a referendum on the soul of the club — member-owned socios democracy versus creeping privatization. Riquelme's campaign originated and amplified this lens, warning that this could be 'the last election' before external shareholders gain a foothold. Pérez countered that the 5% sale is a valuation mechanism, not a loss of control.
framings.emphasizes: Pérez's confirmed intent to sell a 5% stake, the 124-year member-ownership tradition, Riquelme's 'privatization' warnings, and the precedent set by Premier League club ownership models.
framings.downplays: Pérez's argument that the sale empowers socios as formal financial owners; the relatively small size of the proposed stake; the Electoral Board's rejection of Riquelme's process complaints.

framings.name: Incumbency Power & Institutional Entrenchment
framings.question: Does Pérez's unbroken dominance — 23 of 26 years as president, five consecutive uncontested elections — reflect healthy leadership or dangerous concentration of power?
framings.key_claim: Pérez's structural grip on Real Madrid — including his refusal to debate, control of the electoral machinery, and 20-year run without a challenger — represents an entrenched power structure that the 35% Riquelme vote signals members are beginning to question.
framings.description: This framing scrutinizes the conditions that allowed Pérez to run unopposed for five consecutive cycles and asks whether the club's governance rules are designed to protect incumbents. It highlights Pérez's refusal to debate, his use of club legends as campaign props, and Riquelme's allegations about informal power held by Pérez associate Anas Laghrari.
framings.emphasizes: Five uncontested elections, refusal to debate, strict candidacy barriers, Laghrari's informal influence, Riquelme's 35% as a protest vote signal.
framings.downplays: Pérez's genuine trophy record, the Electoral Board's independence, and the fact that Riquelme accepted the result and congratulated Pérez.

framings.name: Generational Change & Reform Momentum
framings.question: Does Riquelme's 35% showing — despite being a 37-year-old unknown challenging a 79-year-old institution — signal a rising reform movement within Real Madrid?
framings.key_claim: Riquelme's credible 35% vote share, backed by legends Raúl, Casillas, and Hierro, marks the emergence of a genuine reform constituency inside Real Madrid that will outlast this election.
framings.description: This framing treats the election not as a Pérez victory but as a Riquelme debut — focusing on the challenger's surprising strength, his backing from club legends, his 'this is the beginning' concession speech, and the prospect of a future run. It frames the result as a generational fault line opening inside the club.
framings.emphasizes: Riquelme's 35% share, his youth (37 vs. Pérez's 79), the Raúl/Casillas/Hierro endorsements, his 'this is not the end' concession, and his five-year preparation claim.
framings.downplays: Pérez's decisive margin, the rejection of Riquelme's electoral complaints, and the implausibility of some of Riquelme's transfer promises.

framings.name: Galáctico Spectacle & Transfer Theater
framings.question: Were the competing transfer and managerial promises — Mourinho vs. Klopp, Haaland vs. Konaté — serious sporting strategy or electoral showmanship?
framings.key_claim: Both candidates turned the election into a transfer auction — Pérez with a secret €150m Galáctico and Mourinho, Riquelme with notarized Haaland guarantees — reducing a governance contest to a fantasy football spectacle.
framings.description: A more skeptical framing, prominent in fan media and analytical outlets, that treats the competing big-name promises as performative electioneering. It notes that Haaland's camp laughed off Riquelme's pledge, Manchester City threatened legal action, and Pérez's mystery €150m signing was deliberately unnamed for maximum suspense.
framings.emphasizes: The notarized Haaland guarantee, Man City's legal threat, the unnamed €150m signing, Mourinho's campaign video ('So MOUch history to be made'), and the comparison to Pérez's 2000 Figo pledge.
framings.downplays: The genuine governance and ownership debates; treats both candidates' promises with equal skepticism.

framings.name: Institutional Continuity & Legacy Mandate
framings.question: Does Pérez's re-election confirm that Real Madrid's members trust his long-term vision and trophy-winning track record above all alternatives?
framings.key_claim: With 65% of the vote and the second-best result in club electoral history, Pérez received a clear mandate from members who credit him with seven Champions Leagues and the Bernabéu renovation.
framings.description: The pro-continuity framing, most visible in Pérez's own communications and sympathetic coverage, emphasizes the scale of his victory, his trophy record, and the club's global prestige under his stewardship. It treats the election as a ratification of an era rather than a rebuke.
framings.emphasizes: 65% vote share, seven Champions Leagues, the Bernabéu renovation, Pérez's claim of the 'second-best result in club electoral history,' and the backing of legends like Ronaldo Nazário and Roberto Carlos.
framings.downplays: The two-season trophy drought, the privatization controversy, the 35% protest vote, and the 20-year absence of competition.

framings.name: Spanish Football Identity & National Team Disconnect
framings.question: Has Pérez's era — with its Super League ambitions and Galáctico globalism — eroded Real Madrid's role as the backbone of the Spanish national team?
framings.key_claim: Spain's World Cup squad named without a single Real Madrid player for the first time in history, a fact Riquelme weaponized to argue that Pérez's global-brand strategy has come at the cost of the club's Spanish footballing soul.
framings.description: A framing specific to the Spanish football ecosystem but amplified in English-language coverage: the election as a proxy debate over whether Real Madrid should prioritize global commercial prestige or its historic role as the engine of La Roja. Riquelme explicitly promised to 're-establish the club as a key feeder for the national team.'
framings.emphasizes: Spain's World Cup squad with no Real Madrid players, Riquelme's 'Spanish identity' platform, his promise of a Spanish World Cup player signing, and the Super League's perceived damage to UEFA relationships.
framings.downplays: The broader squad-building context (injuries, Mbappé's form), Pérez's own Spanish signings over the years, and the fact that national team selection is the coach's prerogative.

gap_analysis: Missing are framings centered on: (1) fan democracy and membership participation—how accessible was voting to ordinary socios, and what does low/high turnout signal about engagement?; (2) financial sustainability and debt management—Pérez's fiscal record and whether re-election represents prudent stewardship or reckless spending; (3) women's football and institutional equity—Real Madrid's investment in or neglect of its women's team as a governance priority; (4) labor and worker perspectives—stadium staff, academy coaches, and player welfare under Pérez's tenure. Also absent: any framing from Riquelme's specific platform or the substantive policy differences between candidates beyond personality.
